subject.title: QMD memory indexing can recurse into symlink loops in workspace-visible temp monorepos and fail with ENAMETOOLONG

question: Should OpenClaw resolve #54463 by requiring/probing a QMD scanner version that skips symlinks, or by owning QMD collection traversal/exclusion before invoking `qmd update`?
rationale: Current upstream QMD appears to have safer traversal, but OpenClaw delegates to user-installed QMD binaries and has no version gate, probe, or own QMD traversal contract; choosing that boundary is a maintainer product decision.

options.title: Gate and probe QMD first
options.body: Require or detect a QMD version with cycle-safe scanning, add doctor/docs follow-through, and only add OpenClaw guards if supported installs remain vulnerable.

options.title: Own the traversal guard
options.body: Add an OpenClaw QMD collection guard or exclusion mechanism before `qmd update`, with tests proving symlink loops cannot expand.

options.title: Keep documented limitation
options.body: Leave behavior as a known limitation and rely on docs telling users to keep temp monorepos outside indexed QMD roots.

recommendation.title: Gate and probe QMD first
recommendation.body: Require or detect a QMD version with cycle-safe scanning, add doctor/docs follow-through, and only add OpenClaw guards if supported installs remain vulnerable.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the issue assignee and shipped the current QMD symlink-limit documentation after deciding the runtime problem was still open.
